questions.title: 62. Controlled vs uncontrolled components?
questions.summary:
◦ Controlled → R^ state owns input value.
◦ Uncontrolled → DOM owns current input value.
questions.answer:
◦ Controlled C^ → Input value is driven by R^ state.
◦ Uses value + onChange + setState to synchronize UI.
◦ Uncontrolled C^ → DOM manages current input value.
◦ Uses defaultValue for initial value + ref to read current value.
◦ Controlled → Best for live validation, conditional UI, and dependent fields.
◦ Uncontrolled → Useful for simple forms and DOM-managed integrations.
◦ Both approaches can be valid depending on requirements.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ Controlled → State update schedules re-r().
◦ R^ supplies updated value to DOM input during commit.
◦ Uncontrolled → Browser updates DOM input directly as user types.
◦ Reading ref.current.value retrieves its current value w/o requiring R^ state.
◦ defaultValue initializes an uncontrolled input but does not continuously control it.
◦ File inputs are inherently uncontrolled for their selected files.
pitfalls: ◦ Controlled input needs onChange or another update mechanism unless readOnly.
◦ Avoid switching between controlled and uncontrolled modes.
◦ value={undefined} can accidentally make an input uncontrolled.
◦ useRef changes do not trigger re-r().
followUps: ◦ How do you avoid controlled/uncontrolled warnings?
questions.recall:
◦ Controlled → State → value + onChange → re-r().
◦ Uncontrolled → DOM → defaultValue + ref.
◦ useState → reactive UI.
◦ useRef → DOM access w/o re-r().

questions.title: 63. How do React forms work?
questions.summary:
◦ R^ forms use native HTML controls + event handlers.
◦ Values can be managed through state or read from the DOM.
questions.answer:
◦ R^ forms use native HTML form elements and R^ event handlers.
◦ Inputs can be controlled through state or uncontrolled through the DOM.
◦ onChange handles user input updates.
◦ onSubmit handles form submission.
◦ event.preventDefault() prevents native navigation when handling submission manually.
◦ FormData can extract named form field values.
◦ Validation can use HTML constraints, custom logic, or schemas.
◦ Submission may trigger async requests, loading states, and error handling.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ R^ registers event handlers through its event system.
◦ Input events invoke handlers that may schedule state updates.
◦ Controlled values are synchronized during rendering and commit.
◦ Native form submission follows browser behavior unless intercepted.
◦ FormData reads successful named controls from the form.
◦ React 19 supports form action F()s and useActionState for action-related state.
pitfalls: ◦ Missing name attributes cause fields to be absent from FormData.
◦ preventDefault() is unnecessary when intentionally using native or supported form actions.
◦ Client-side validation does not replace server-side validation.
◦ Handle pending, success, and error states.
◦ Disabled controls are excluded from FormData.
followUps: ◦ How does React 19 form action work?
questions.recall:
◦ Input → onChange → State/DOM.
◦ Submit → onSubmit → Validate → Process.
◦ FormData → Named fields.
◦ React 19 → Form Actions + useActionState.

questions.title: 64. How do you implement a controlled form?
questions.summary:
◦ Store field values in useState.
◦ Bind value + onChange + onSubmit to manage input and submission.
questions.answer:
◦ Initialize form values using useState.
◦ Bind each input value to state.
◦ Use onChange to update the corresponding field.
◦ Update object state immutably using the spread operator.
◦ Use onSubmit to validate and process the form.
◦ Prevent native submission when handling it manually.
◦ Display validation errors and submission status through state.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ User types → Browser dispatches input event.
◦ R^ invokes onChange handler.
◦ setState enqueues an update.
◦ R^ schedules and processes re-r().
◦ New state produces updated input props.
◦ Commit synchronizes controlled input value w1 DOM.
◦ State becomes the authoritative source for displayed input values.
pitfalls: ◦ Do not mutate form state directly.
◦ Avoid missing onChange for controlled inputs.
◦ Use stable initial values, such as empty strings.
◦ Ensure input name matches the state field key.
◦ Avoid logging passwords or other sensitive form data.
followUps: ◦ How do you manage multiple inputs?
◦ How do you handle async submission?
◦ Controlled forms vs React Hook Form?
questions.recall:
◦ useState → value → onChange → setState → re-r().
◦ onSubmit → Validate → Submit.
◦ Spread → Immutable update.
◦ State = Single source of truth.
